[Arrays 1 — line, grid, cube, curve]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/overview/#b04) · class 1 of 1

Submit 2.1 by 11:59 PM. Build a loop and a nested loop — a 1D row, a 2D grid, then 3D layers — then bend the row onto a curve and stack it into a brick wall, on a curve or a circle. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction. Check your CSG print file before queueing it.

## Example files

Build your own file. Use these examples to check a step when you are stuck, then return to your work. Do not submit the example files unchanged. Designated Project 4 analysis, volume and contouring groups may be reused directly in your own project. Select the lesson object; press Home over the node editor to see the graph. Follow the Frames in order. Change inputs on the nodes or, where provided, in the GeometryNodes modifier.

Prepared in **Blender 5.2.1 LTS**. Earlier Blender versions may lack the volume nodes used in the later classes.

**[Arrays — Part 1: line, grid, cube, curve, wall]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/03-arrays-lists/Arrays-Lists-Session-1.blend)** — download .blend

1. Linear loop
2. Nested grid
3. 3D array
4. Along a curve
5. Brick wall

**Practice:** Repeat the previous geometry along a line and across a grid, then extend the grid into layers. Bend the row onto a curve, then stack it into a wall with odd courses shifted. Identify count, spacing and index in each direction.
